Hallo Susanne,

es kann durchaus sei, dass dein Postfachanbieter eine maximale Aufbewahrungsfrist von soundsoviel Tagen anwendet, nach der die älteren Nachrichten automatisch vom Server gelöscht werden. Das würde sich bei dir in Thunderbird aber nur dann auswirken, wenn es sich um ein IMAP konnte handelt. Also erste Frage: handelt es sich bei dem betroffenen Konto um ein POP- oder ein IMAP Konto? Wenn es sich um ein IMAP Konto handelt, dann sind die verschwundenen Nachrichten weg, es sei denn der Postfachanbieter macht dir ein Geschenk 😀 Bei POP Konten in Thunderbird ist die Gefahr des automatischen Löschens von alten Nachrichten praktisch ausgeschlossen, da sie lokal gespeichert sind und die Standard-Einstellungen kein automatisches Löschen auf dem PC vorsehen. Natürlich ist das keine Gewähr gegen ein unabsichtliches Löschen durch den Benutzer, und die meisten Nachrichtenverluste entstehen durch fehlerhafte Aktionen.

Falls du POP benutzt, kannst du durchaus bei beendetem Thunderbird die Datei Inbox.msf im Profilordner von Thunderbird löschen. Letztere ist die Index-Datei deines Posteingang-Ordners, welche keine Nachrichten enthält. Im Gegensatz zur Mailbox-Datei Inbox (ohne Endung!), in der die Mails deines Posteingangs gespeichert sind. Ich bin aber etwas vorsichtig, diese Aktion des Löschens der Inbox.msf zu befürworten, wenn Benutzer nicht vertraut sind mit dem Profilordner. Wenn du es trotzdem wagen willst, bekommst du eine kleine Anleitung.

Dass dein Posteingang durch die "Reparieren" Aktion von 900 MB auf 5 MB geschwunden ist, kann ich nicht erklären. Beim Reparieren wird nur die Index-Datei Inbox.msf neu erstellt, aber nichts an der Mailbox-Datei Inbox selbst geändert, welche deine Nachrichten enthält. Hast du vielleicht "Reparieren" mit "Komprimieren" verwechselt?

"Löschen" einer Nachricht bedeutet nämlich nur, dass sie zunächst nicht mehr im Ordner in Thunderbird sichtbar ist (aber sofort in den Papierkorb "verschoben wird). In der Datei Inbox wird lediglich der sogenannte X-Mozilla-Status der Nachricht auf "gelöscht" geändert, woraufhin sofort die Inbox.msf Index-Datei dahingehend geändert wird, dass die Nachricht nicht mehr in Thunderbird sichtbar ist. Erst beim Komprimieren des Posteingangs werden dann die nach dem Löschen noch in der Datei Inbox verbliebenen Nachrichten-Texte entfernt.

In deinem Screenshot ist die Datei Inbox.msf an der Spitze der Liste von unmittelbarer Bedeutung, da sie das Datum von heute hat und eine Größe von nur 45 kB. content:
It is very possible to have to Thunderbird installations in different locations. For example, one could be a 32-bit version and the other a 64-bit. Or one could have been from an official Thunderbird installer and the other from the Microsoft Store. Unless there's some specific reason to have both, it's a waste of disk space and confusing. I would make a safety backup of my Profile, uninstall both existing installations, and re-install using an official installer from

https://www.thunderbird.net/

Here's how I would go about it. This is Windows 10, but it should be similar on 11, maybe some names are slightly different:

- Make a safety backup of my profile. To do that, open Windows File Explorer and in the address bar, type $APPDATA$ . This will take you to your AppData folder where there are sub-folders for many or most of your various installed programs. One will be called "Thunderbird". While Thunderbird is closed, make a copy of that folder to a convenient location (Desktop?)

- Now go to Windows' <Settings | Apps and Features>. You should see two entries for Thunderbird, similar to the attached image. Uninstall them both, perhaps starting with the older version. The uninstall should leave your Profile in place, but you have a backup of it just in case.

- Reboot (probably not necessary, but it can't hurt.)

- Now run the installer you downloaded earlier. If all goes well, it will see your Profile in the default location and you should be back in the saddle again. If not, it's easily fixable.

- If things are back to normal, you can delete the safety copy of your Profile, or better yet, save it as a backup and start making regular backups of the original folder. They can be ZIP compressed to save space. But that's another topic.

Please let me know how it goes.

content:
If you are seeing the message on the status bar, likely it is Tbird telling you that it has deleted its copy of the messages when synchronizing with the server. Because you're accessing by IMAP, Tbird is trying to mirror what's in your mailbox at your ISP. That's one of the fundamentals of IMAP--make the mailbox in your client software (in this case, Tbird), match what's on the server.

I see that message often when I open the Trash folder in my IMAP account. My ISP purges "deleted" messages older than two weeks, but I rarely open the Trash folder, which only synchronizes when I open it.

I'm assuming this is happening in the inbox for your IMAP account, which suggests to me that something outside of Tbird is manipulating your mailbox.

Do you access your email from another device--another computer, a phone, a tablet, etc.? Or my logging into a web mail program? Could one of those be filing your mail or treating it as spam? Does someone/something else have access to your mailbox on your behalf?

If you can't think of any way that someone or something else should be manipulating your mailbox, I'd recommend you change the password ASAP and update it in Tbird. See if the deletions stop. If so, then one-by-one, update the password in your other devices to see if one of them may be making changes.

content:
IMAP account can only show whatever is on the server. All folders in an Imap account synchronise with folders of same name on server.

'What can cause a deletion of emails in an IMAP account:'

Other than user selecting and deleting emails manually.

If you access the webmail account via a browser and delete emails then when Thunderbird accesses server those emails will get deleted in order to match the server.

It is also the same if you access the same account via another device eg: laptop, tablet, phone, another desktop computer and delete emails. So check settings etc in all devices that access the same account.

IF you have another device accessing mail eg: phone and it's set up as POP, then maybe it's been set up to download and delete off server - it would need to have settings 'Leave messages on server'. If the POP account is deleting upon download then those emails are no longer on server, so when IMAP account synchronises - those emails previously seen in IMAP will get deleted.

Did you ever set up to view emails in another email client eg: Outlook ? If yes, please check your computer because it might still be running in the background. If it has anything set up to delete emails then it could be the cause of the problem.

Many servers do remove emails from 'Spam' and 'Trash' periodically. When email has been in eg: Trash for 30 days it gets auto deleted off server. Some servers it's 30 days others 14 and I've also come across some that do 7 days and even 3 days.

Are you talking about an AOL account? If yes, are you accessing via the Yahoo server ?

Please note AOL say: By default, both the Trash and Spam folders empty automatically to keep your account tidy. These settings are set systemically and can't be changed. • Trash deletion frequency - Trash is deleted after 7 days. • Spam deletion frequency - Spam is deleted after 30 days.

  • https://help.aol.com/articles/spam-and-trash-folders-are-regularly-deleted-in-aol-mail

How to auto delete emails in Thunderbird - so check these locations: In Thunderbird 'Account Settings'

  • 'Server Settings' for the imap account
  • look bottom right under 'Message Storage'

have you set up to 'Empty Deleted folder on Exit' ? If yes then anything in 'Trash/Deleted' folder will get emptied automatically on exit.

  • 'Spam Settings' for the imap account
  • look bottom right under 'Destination and Retention'

Have you selected 'Automatically delete spam mail older than X days' ? If yes, then you might be seeing this auto deletion notification.

  • 'Synchronisation & Storage' for the imap account
  • Under Disc Space:
  • Select 'Don't delete any messages'


It would have useful if you could tell us more about the folder name that emails are being deleted from. But Check folders:

  • Right click on folder and select 'Properties'
  • Select 'Retention Policy' tab
  • It's usual to select 'Use my account settings'

But do make sure the account settings are not set up to delete anything.

Have you created any Message Filters ? If yes:

  • do any of them mention move to folder that is not in the Imap account ?
  • Do any mention the word 'delete' in the perform this action ?


You mention you get a message about emails being deleted, but what you do not say is what folder are they being deleted from. I think it would be very obvious if they were being deleted from eg: Inbox, so I'm surprised you never mentioned it. That makes me wonder if it's the Trash or Spam folder.

Are you by any chance still using CCeaner ? https://www.ccleaner.com/legal/products-policy?srsltid=AfmBOoqrRCFu6i8HU9W-VjWcW2O93fH5TnB1y1TQhV4qvbEKI335rN9-

If yes, then you need to make sure it's not allowed to access your Thunderbird profile name folder and do not allow it to control updates. In other words Exclude the thunderbird profile folder from any access /scan etc.

It can cause havoc. It can delete files you need. You might even find it removing stored passwords, cookies, cache, and anything stored in temp files. CCleaner is well known for being a problem when it comes to email clients.

Windows and CCleaner must not be allowed to perform updates when it comes to Thunderbird as you may get the wrong one. Only allow Thunderbird to perform updates. There are various channels and they get different updates and sometimes Thunderbird deliberately does not update when significant new alterations have occurred, but CCleaner like other Updater programs do not have any comprehension regarding the situation.
